query: Consider the following context: Non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are promising candidates for low-dimensional magnetocaloric applications. In that context, which method can be used for tuning the magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Altering the composition via targeted chemical substitution in non-equiatomic HEAs can tune the magnetic ordering temperature and thereby modify the magnetocaloric effect.
generation.material_initial_state: A non-equiatomic high-entropy alloy with a baseline, single-phase microstructure.
generation.intervention: Introduce controlled chemical substitutions by partially replacing one or more of the transition metal elements.
generation.conditions: Samples are prepared under identical processing conditions (e.g., melting, annealing) to isolate the effect of chemical substitution while maintaining a single-phase microstructure in a low-dimensional system.
generation.structural_mediator: Local atomic environments and magnetic exchange interactions which are affected by the substitution, altering magnetic anisotropy and ordering.
generation.mechanism: The substitution changes the balance of magnetic exchange interactions—modifying both the magnetic moment and ordering temperature—which in turn adjusts the magnitude and temperature range of the magnetocaloric effect.
generation.predicted_outcome: An alloy with an optimally substituted composition will exhibit a shifted magnetic ordering temperature and an enhanced magnetocaloric effect compared to the original non-equiatomic HEA.
generation.baseline: The original non-equiatomic HEA composition without substitution.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is applicable within the compositional regime that maintains a single-phase HEA structure and is limited to low-dimensional systems where magnetocaloric properties are prominent.
generation.uncertainty: It is uncertain how specific elemental substitutions will quantitatively influence the magnetic interactions and ordering temperature without targeted experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a series of non-equiatomic HEA samples with incremental substitution of one magnetic element (e.g., replacing a fraction of the element with another having different magnetic characteristics) under identical processing conditions. Measure the magnetic ordering temperature and magnetocaloric effect for each composition.
measurements: Magnetization vs. temperature (to determine the magnetic ordering temperature)
Isothermal magnetization curves (to evaluate the magnetocaloric effect)
Direct measurement of temperature change under applied magnetic fields
Microstructural characterization to ensure a single-phase structure
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the compositional modifications do not lead to any measurable shift in the magnetic ordering temperature or a significant change in the magnitude of the magnetocaloric effect compared to the baseline HEA, then the hypothesis is falsified.
